name: CDFW Restoration Grant Programs

funder.name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

summary: California state grants, through a continuous concept-proposal process, for restoration of wetlands, mountain meadows, rivers, streams and habitat, covering planning, implementation and acquisition projects.

eligibility.rule: For Mojave funding, the project is not a research project
Acquisitions use willing sellers and DGS-approved fair market value
Multiple-landowner projects have written permission from all landowners or a designee
Use a California-licensed engineer or geologist where legally required
Comply with applicable state, tribal and federal environmental laws
Obtain all permits necessary to complete the project work
Hold a valid collection permit when collecting protected wildlife or plants
Not a private individual, for-profit enterprise, or out-of-state public entity except the stated exceptions

documents: 65% or higher design plans for implementation projects
Basis of design report for implementation projects
Proposed site access agreement template, if site access is not held
Memorandum of understanding, if site access is not held
Landowner permission form, if site access is not held
Purchase option agreement or willing seller letter for acquisitions
Water right permit or license for post-1914 water rights
Evidence of diversion right and priority for riparian or pre-1914 rights

applicant_types.quote: eligible applicants for funding include: Tribes, nonprofit organizations and public agencies.

access.quote: The application process begins with a concept proposal submitted through CDFW's WebGrants(opens in new tab) portal.

geography.quote: to accelerate the pace and scale of restoration throughout the state

co_finance_required.quote: Cost share is not required to be eligible for funding but is encouraged and will benefit project review and selection.

eligibility.quote: Research projects are not eligible for funding through this solicitation.
Acquisitions must be from willing sellers and at fair market value, as confirmed by an appraisal approved by the Department of General Services (DGS) Real Property Services Section.
For projects involving multiple landowners, all landowners or an appointed designee must provide written permission to complete the project.
Some projects require a California licensed professional engineer or California licensed professional geologist to comply with applicable requirements of the Business and Professions Code
Projects must comply with all applicable state, tribal, and federal environmental laws and regulations.
Applicants are responsible for obtaining all permits necessary to complete project work.
Projects that involve the collection of fish, wildlife, or endangered or rare plants must have a valid collection permit.

Proposals from private individuals, for-profit enterprises (unless where eligible for funding as a public utility), or outof-state public entities (except those that are nonprofit organizations registered with the California Secretary of State) are ineligible for funding

after_award.quote: Grantees shall submit progress reports as outlined in the executed grant agreement to the CDFW grant manager for the duration of the grant.

documents.quote: Applicants should demonstrate land tenure, CEQA compliance, and submit 65% or higher design plans, a basis of design report, and technical studies.

When an applicant does not have land tenure/site access at the time of proposal submission, the applicant must submit a proposed site access agreement template, memorandum of understanding, or landowner permission form with the proposal.

For projects involving multiple landowners, all landowners or an appointed designee must provide written permission to complete the project. Acquisition proposals must include a signed purchase option agreement or willing seller letter from each landowner indicating that they are a willing participant in the proposed real estate transaction.

For post-1914 water rights, the applicant must submit a copy of a water right permit or license on file with the SWRCB. Applicants who divert water based on a riparian or pre-1914 water right must submit written evidence of the right to divert water and the priority in the watershed of that diversion right with their proposal.

effort.quote: Applicants will first submit a concept proposal.
Depending on the funding program, CDFW may request supplemental information (e.g., bond funding) or a full application (e.g., FRGP)

steps: Full application or supplemental information, if requested
